captions: Jacques Lusseyran runs through Paris before a childhood accident leaves his eyes bandaged. Panels of hands touching a cup, a window and a book use golden lines to introduce the comic’s inner-light motif.
Under the occupation of France, Lusseyran listens as students gather around papers. The sequence moves from marching figures in the street to quiet meetings and his hands finding a wall at night.
Lusseyran and fellow Resistance members meet by candlelight, print leaflets and pass papers between doorways. Close-ups of listening faces connect their underground work with trust and attention.
A meeting gives way to a police raid, questioning and a crowded deportation train. A golden line follows Lusseyran’s hand against the train’s wooden interior.
At Buchenwald, prisoners stand outside barracks, whisper to one another and offer a supporting hand. The final group gathers around a small light, continuing the comic’s image of solidarity.
The sequence turns from camp memories to manuscripts, a classroom and Lusseyran speaking to students. An illuminated book connects his writing and teaching with the experiences he survived.
A road scene and an empty chair mark Lusseyran’s death in 1971. Candles, pages and a group of readers revisit his life, ending with attention as the comic’s lasting theme.
